findings.reason: a node following the named source would add a discard check to a rollback helper that never runs on the successful-launch path, while the function it was told to stop over is the one that actually launches, so the node would either spend its gate discovering the misdirection or stop blocked.
findings.text: §61 states the launch of an already-discarded request "named the source: `_release_launch_claim`", but that function (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:816) runs only on a refused dispatch's rollback (`_claim_released_on_refusal`, dispatch.py:2997) and `promotion.discard` never calls it; the section's own launch path is `_launch_queued` (queue_admission.py:195) → `dispatch` → `_publish_launch_claim` (dispatch_claims.py:754), none of which consults `discard_recorded`, and `queue_admission.py` is excluded from §61's write paths by its own blocked rule.
